Identifies whether an employee is a non-seasonal, full-time, permanent employee. This variable was created to address an interior coverage gap in the nsftp_indicator variable. It takes a value of 1 if the work schedule is full-time (work_schedule_code is F, which excludes seasonal schedules) and the appointment type is permanent (codes 10, 15, 30, 32, 34, 35, 36, 38, 50, 55); 0 otherwise; and NA where work_schedule_code is unknown. The OPM nsftp_indicator is only 1 when work_schedule_code is F; however, it is sometimes 1 for appointment_type_codes that map to sentinel values (e.g., **) or to nonpermanent types. To create a consistent variable across the full panel, we use the definition above. We also assume that the permanent codes from 1982 and later are permanent codes before 1982 as well, when no publicly available labels for the appointment_type_codes exist. We confirmed that the FWOC variable produces no false positives: it is never 1 when the OPM indicator is 0. Examination of how work schedules and appointment types map to the OPM indicator prior to 1982 reveals that appointment type code 40 included a roughly 50-50 mix of permanent and non-permanent appointment types. Before 1982, the FWOC indicator undercounts NSFTP employees in code 40 -- which is labeled SCHEDULE A (EXCEPTED SERVICE NONPERMANENT) after 1982 -- by about 472,000 of 885,000 full-time code-40 observations (53%) that carry OPM nsftp=1 but are coded 0 by the FWOC version, roughly 0.8% of all pre-1982 nsftp observations. After 1982, when code 40 is cleanly non-permanent, this undercount is negligible (~1,100). In short, this is the cost of filling the coverage gap.

OPM did not publish the occupational category (PATCO) for the data.opm.gov (FWD) era from 2005-03 through 2009-12, leaving occupational_category_code blank for those years. This variable fills that gap and applies one uniform rule across the full 1973-present panel, so the series-to-category mapping is consistent over time. It is built from a per-(year, month) crosswalk: the 2005-2009 gap is sourced from the raw BuzzFeed FOIA status data, and every other period from the published occupational_category_code itself. The crosswalk maps occupational_series_code to a single category wherever that is unambiguous; for the series whose category is not a function of the series alone (e.g. 0303, which spans both Technical and Clerical), it uses the finer (occupational_series_code, pay_plan_code, grade) combination. About 2% of rows fall in combinations that still do not resolve to a single PATCO category; these are left blank rather than imputed. The blanking applies in every period, so this variable is not a superset of the unedited column -- from 2010 on, occupational_category_code may carry a value where occupational_category_code_fwoc is blank. The unresolved combinations are listed in metadata/crosswalks/occ_series_patco_unresolved.csv in the GitHub repository. This variable covers the employment data only; we do not apply the mapping to the accessions/separations datasets, which are sparse flows whose first-of-month labeling would inherit the employment as-of code with added slippage -- users who want PATCO there can apply the published crosswalk themselves. For OPM's exact, per-position published values, use occupational_category_code.
